subject: Pilot scope: latency sensitivity & capacity path for FastLedger
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-08-03T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot scope: latency sensitivity & capacity path for FastLedger

Hi Laura — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment going into a pilot.

Call highlights (short):
- Goal: user-facing personalization API for checkout recommendations (model: 6B decoders)
- Current signals: steady qps ~80, peak bursts to ~360 for 30–90s at ~3 times per hour; p95 latency target ~<120ms end-to-end
- Security note: FastLedger has PCI-adjacent constraints; you noted a preference for private VPC if we can’t meet SLOs on hosted.

Redwood read on tradeoffs (very condensed):
- Hosted API: fastest to start, flexible autoscaling, good for spiky traffic if bursts are short and cacheable; potential tail-latency variability under extreme concurrent bursts
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools give predictable p95/p99 behavior for sustained throughput, better for long (>10m) sustained peaks and stricter SLO guarantees
- Private/VPC: required only if there are hard compliance blockers — otherwise cost and ops are higher

Proposed next steps (pick 1–2):
1) Run a 2-week hosted pilot with our burst-capacity profile + tracing to see tail latency under real traffic. We can gate to Dedicated if p95 exceeds 140ms on pilot traffic.
2) If you prefer definitive SLOs up front, map to Dedicated capacity with a 30-day evaluation (we’ll size based on the pilot signals).

Asks from our side to scope the pilot:
- Sample traces or a 24h qps distribution (we only need a small CSV or histogram)
- A representative request payload / average tokens per request
- Any hard compliance items (examples: SOC/SRS references, specific KMS/HSM requirements)

Attachments: call-recording-20270803.mp3 (audio), prelim-sla-worksheet.xlsx (worksheet for filling single-day/peak signals).

If you’re comfortable with option 1, we’ll schedule the pilot start and loop in Jasmine (solutions eng) to size the initial cluster and share a short test harness. If you want option 2 now, we’ll size Dedicated and share an estimated committed price.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the traces and your preference.

—Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Peak behavior: the spikes (to ~360 qps) are mostly concentrated during promo windows and last 30–120 seconds; a couple of times per day we see longer bursts (~10 minutes) during scheduled drops.
- Payload size: average request ~420 tokens; worst-case 1.1k tokens (rare).
- Compliance: PCI scoping team asks for encryption-in-transit and audit logs; they want to see access logs from the pilot. We do prefer hosted pilot first but reserve right to request VPC if anything in the logs raises red flags.

Procurement is cc’d — they’ll need pricing and a statement of work for a potential Dedicated commitment if the pilot shows the need. I attached a quick architecture sketch we use internally (architecture-draft.pdf).

Next steps: please send the pilot test harness and a short price range for a 2-week hosted trial + an estimated cost for a Dedicated node equivalent (ballpark). We aim to decide within 10 business days.

—Laura

Quick internal note / proposal before we respond back with pricing: 

Summary of ask from Laura:
- Pilot: 2-week hosted run if they want to start quickly
- Inputs: qps histogram, payload sizes, and audit-log requirement for PCI review
- Decision criterion: if p95 > 140ms under their real traffic we recommend Dedicated sizing

Proposal:
- Offer a hosted pilot configuration that includes:
  * 2x warm-up nodes + autoscaler to 8 nodes for bursts (model: 6B, fp16/quant path)
  * Continuous prefix caching for repeated contexts (should reduce token compute)
  * Tracing + access logs exported to the Drive link they provided for procurement review
- If pilot shows sustained >300 qps for >10 minutes, present a Dedicated sizing estimate (likely 4–6 reserved GPUs depending on memory profile)
- Jasmine to own the pilot test harness and perf gates; Naomi to own pricing + SOC2/PCI audit artifact pull

Action items (internal):
- Jasmine: prep test harness and run an internal dry-run with synthetic spikes to validate autoscaler behavior (ETA 48h)
- Naomi: draft hosted trial SOW + ballpark Dedicated pricing (ETA 24h)
- Marissa: reply to Laura with pilot plan and ask for the traces & sample payloads
